## The SDR Challenge

SDR roles combine high volume, frequent turnover and a direct effect on pipeline. Building a sustainable SDR hiring engine matters for growth companies. This article quotes no turnover or pay figures, because we have not cited a source for any.

### The SDR Profile

Successful SDRs tend to share:

- Resilience and tolerance for rejection
- Coachability and learning agility
- Competitive drive
- Strong verbal communication
- Discipline and work ethic

### Experience Requirements

Consider carefully:

- Little prior experience is often sufficient
- Customer-facing experience, such as retail or restaurants, can be valuable
- Competitive athletes often do well
- Prior sales experience helps but need not be required

### Assessment Methods

**Hiring in Sales?**

[See how TaaSFlow works for sales hiring](/industries/sales)

Beyond interviews:

- Role-play cold calls
- Written email exercises
- Work sample tests
- Structured group assessments

Be careful with personality assessments. Use them only if you can show they relate to the job, and never as a sole screen.

### Compensation Structures

SDR plans usually combine base pay and variable pay, often with accelerators for over-performance. Benchmark against a current, named compensation source.

### Training for Success

Set new SDRs up with:

- A structured ramp
- Call shadowing and reverse shadowing
- Script certification
- Tool training (CRM, sequences)
- An ongoing coaching cadence

### Measuring SDR Hiring Success

Track:

- Ramp time to quota
- Retention at 90 days
- Pipeline generated per hire
- Manager satisfaction
- Promotion rates

### Where TaaSFlow Fits

TaaSFlow is a recruiting platform with managed execution. Agents source and score candidates, a recruiter reviews every shortlist before you see it, and you make every hiring decision. For high-volume SDR hiring, talk to us about scope first. Volume hiring needs a conversation about capacity, so [talk to us about volume hiring](/contact).

Building an SDR team is a marathon, not a sprint. A systematic process is the only sustainable approach.
